cohort: Three patients (a 16-year-old female, a 35-year-old female, and a 36-year-old male) experiencing acute massive hemorrhage who presented to a peripheral hospital with limited blood product resources.
finding: Warm fresh whole blood (WFWB) transfusion effectively stabilized hemodynamic and laboratory parameters, replaced crucial blood components, and prevented complications like hypothermia and dilutional coagulopathy in patients with acute massive hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Two of the three cases involved massive bleeding due to uterine atony during emergency cesarean sections, where WFWB transfusion was successfully used to stabilize the patients.
